tasks.title: Laravel security fix in this repo (project root): centralize the admin authorization logic into config + a Laravel Gate (behavior must stay IDENTICAL). Files: app/Models/Login.php (isAdmin() method, ~lines 155-170), app/Http/Middleware/SystemAccess/RedirectIfNotSystemAdmin.php (handle() calls $request->user()->isAdmin()), app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php (boot() method), config/auth.php. Current isAdmin(): return $user->belongstostaff()->where('authorise_id', 1)->exists() || in_array($user->id, [117, 72]); — the magic values 1 / [117, 72] are hardcoded in the model. Fix: (1) append a small 'admins' block to the existing config/auth.php (editing an existing config file): 'admins' => ['authorise_id' => 1, 'login_ids' => [117, 72]] with a short comment explaining these are the legacy admin markers (authorise_id column on staffs + legacy hardcoded login ids) and the intended migration path is a roles/permissions table later — do NOT build that table now; (2) refactor Login::isAdmin() to read the values from config so the semantics are byte-for-byte identical: $user->belongstostaff()->where('authorise_id', config('auth.admins.authorise_id'))->exists() || in_array($user->id, config('auth.admins.login_ids', [])); (3) in AuthServiceProvider::boot(), register a Gate named 'admin' that delegates to the model: Gate::define('admin', function ($user) { return $user->isAdmin(); }); (uncomment/enable the Gate facade import; keep the existing Auth::provider registration exactly as is); (4) refactor RedirectIfNotSystemAdmin::handle() to use the Gate instead of a direct model call: if (!$request->user() || !$request->user()->can('admin')) { return abort('403'); } — the Login model extends Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\User so can() is available. Do NOT change any other authorization behavior (isHighManagement checks stay untouched), do not create a roles table or migrations, and do not touch the activity-log middleware or any other file. Then run php -l on every changed file and php artisan test to confirm nothing broke.

Write a unit test for the authorization centralization in this repo (project root) and run the test suite. Create tests/Unit/AuthorizationGuardTest.php: a plain PHPUnit test (no database) with source-level guards: (1) read app/Models/Login.php as a string and assert isAdmin() no longer hardcodes the magic values — the file must NOT contain the literal '[117, 72]' and must NOT contain 'authorise_id', 1 (the numeric 1 adjacent to the column), but MUST contain config('auth.admins.authorise_id') and config('auth.admins.login_ids'); (2) read config/auth.php as a string and assert it contains 'admins' => with 'authorise_id' => 1 and 'login_ids' => [117, 72]; (3) read app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php as a string and assert it contains Gate::define('admin'; (4) read app/Http/Middleware/SystemAccess/RedirectIfNotSystemAdmin.php as a string and assert it uses can('admin') (and does not contain a raw isAdmin() call). Run php artisan test — the suite must stay green (currently 35 passing tests / 113 assertions) — and report the run result with the test report contract.
